stories.headline: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake shakes Peru's Andes, with no damage or casualties immediately reported
stories.title: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake shakes Peru's Andes, with no damage or casualties immediately reported
stories.summary: Lima, Nov 21: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake shook the Andes in central Peru on Friday with no immediate reports of damage or casualties. The US Geological Survey said the earthquake struck at 7:09 pm local time (0900 GMT Saturday). Its epicentre was in the Andes, 34 kilometres (21 miles) north of Junin, at a depth of 108 kilometres (67 miles). Peru's Geophysical Institute said no damage or casualties had been reported. The earthquake was felt in the Peruvian capital, prompting residents to rush into the streets. Peru lies along the "Ring of Fire", a 40,000-kilometre (25,000-mile) arc of volcanoes and fault lines around the Pacific Basin, where most of the world's earthquakes occur. In August, a 6.7 magnitude earthquake in the Peruvian Andes left two people injured and damaged several homes, health centres and schools, while in July, a 5.5-magnitude quake in the Junín region resulted in six deaths and 30 injuries.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan: Heavy rain inundates low-lying areas of Ichchapuram, Sompeta in Srikakulam district
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan: Heavy rain inundates low-lying areas of Ichchapuram, Sompeta in Srikakulam district
stories.summary: Ichchapuram records 184.6 mm in 24 hours; the Collector says leave for all officials has been cancelled for relief work
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Srikakulam district has been witnessing heavy rain for the last day under the impact of Cyclone Akvan, which is yet to cross the coast between Ichchapuram in Andhra Pradesh and Gopalpur in Odisha.
The heavy rain inundated many low-lying areas of Ichchapuram, Kaviti, Sompeta and other places close to the sea coast of Srikakulam.
As per the latest data provided by the government, Srikakulam district recorded an average rainfall of 30.3 mm (908.4 mm across its mandals) between 8 a.m. on Thursday and 8 a.m. on Friday.
Ichchapuram received 184.6 mm, followed by Kanchili with 152 mm.
Kaviti got 149.2 mm and Sompeta 130.4 mm, throwing life out of gear for people of the Palasa division.
The district is likely to witness more downpours for the next two days, as per the precautionary guidelines given by the government and the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar, who toured Ichchapuram and other places, said the situation was under control in the district, since many precautionary measures had been taken to mitigate the impact of the cyclone.
He said leave for all officials and staff had been cancelled so that they could take part in relief operations in Ichchapuram and other nearby mandals.
He said the Bahuda and other rivers might receive 30,000 cusecs of water because of heavy rain in their catchment areas in Odisha.
The district administration was coordinating closely with Odisha officials to monitor the flood situation, given the floods in the Bahuda a month ago, he said.
Mr. Swapnil said the enumeration of crop damage would be taken up in a few days.

Paryavarana Parirakshana Sangham leader and Jyotirao Phule Backward Classes Association State president Beena Dhilli Rao urged the government to appoint a high-level committee of experts and officials to study ways to protect people of Ichchapuram, Sompeta and other places that are regularly affected by natural calamities.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan weakens: Kolkata to see heavy rain till Saturday, relief from Tuesday
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan weakens: Kolkata to see heavy rain till Saturday, relief from Tuesday
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan's impact continues to disrupt weather conditions across Bengal, with Kolkata witnessing waterlogging and traffic disruptions.
The IMD has warned of further heavy rainfall in several South Bengal districts.

Kolkata: Continuous rainfall under the influence of Cyclone Akvan has disrupted normal life across Kolkata and several districts of South Bengal, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warning of further heavy to very heavy showers in parts of the state.
With overcast skies and persistent rain showing little sign of easing, residents of Kolkata are likely to face another difficult day on Saturday, November 21.
The weather system has already weakened after crossing the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast near Gopalpur on Friday morning.
According to the IMD, Akvan crossed the coast between 7.30 am and 8.30 am before weakening into a deep depression over south coastal Odisha by 11.30 am.
It is moving north-northeastwards across Odisha and is expected to weaken further into a depression before becoming a well-marked low-pressure area.
However, the weakening of the system has not brought immediate relief to Bengal.
Kolkata recorded around 38 mm of rainfall, with several neighbourhoods witnessing water accumulation.
Areas including Bhowanipore, Patuli, Thanthania, Salt Lake, New Town, College Street and Amherst Street reported waterlogging during Friday morning.
The Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) deployed jet-cum-suction machines to clear accumulated water and monitored the situation through its integrated control room.
Civic authorities also tracked incidents involving fallen trees.

stories.headline: CONMEBOL backs Infantino re-election bid with ‘strong support’
stories.title: CONMEBOL backs Infantino re-election bid with ‘strong support’
stories.summary: Infantino faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he also retains support from Africa and Asia for his bid to win re-election next March.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has “unanimous” backing for reelection as head of world football from CONMEBOL, the ten-country South American bloc said Friday.
Infantino faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he also retains support from Africa and Asia for his bid to win re-election next March.
Each country has one vote with 211 members and the winner will need to secure at least 106 votes in the ballot scheduled for March 18 in Rabat.
Conmebol has 10, Africa has 54 and Asia 46.
The CONMEBOL statement was made at Barranquilla ahead of Saturday’s Copa Sudamericana final between Brazil’s Atletico Mineiro and Argentina’s Boca Juniors.
CONMEBOL said it appreciated “the leadership of the current FIFA president” and the “positive transformations in football” that he has driven since taking office in 2016.
Having been the sole candidate in 2019 and 2023, Infantino faces two declared challengers: Frenchman Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima.

Infantino has fended off criticism of the enlargement of the World Cup, giving a FIFA Peace Prize to Donald Trump and -- at the American president’s request -- overturning a red card for a US player during the competition.
Infantino is under severe pressure for the first time, but mainly due to UEFA’s reaction to the private investor plan that forced his humiliating climbdown.
UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has given full backing to Diallo, while Tashima has pledged to restore “integrity” to world football’s governing body.
Tashima, who serves on the FIFA Council, stressed his intention to restore trust in the governing body and make transparency and integrity the hallmarks of his campaign.
He said he decided to run after he was incensed by FIFA’s shock decision to lift the ban on United States player Folarin Balogun.

stories.headline: India says no change in its position on IWT as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
stories.title: India says no change in its position on IWT as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 20: India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) is "very clear" and there has been "absolutely no change" in it, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday, amid a visit by Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi. Malik, who arrived here in the early hours of Friday, attended the opening day of the three-day forum in the evening. The event, being hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. India had announced on October 28 that invitations had been extended to all SCO members, including Pakistan, in keeping with established practice. It was perhaps the first time New Delhi had invited a Pakistani minister to attend an event in India since the May 7-10 military hostilities last year following Operation Sindoor. Pakistan had announced on November 14 that its Climate Change Minister Malik would participate in the forum. At his bi-weekly media briefing, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked how New Delhi viewed Malik's participation in the India-hosted forum, given that he does not hold the culture portfolio and had reportedly made comments on the IWT. "As far as IWT is concerned, we have made our position very clear, and that is where it remains. There is absolutely no change," Jaiswal said. India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives. Malik's participation in the forum is being seen by some experts as an opportunity in a multilateral framework that may help improve ties between the two neighbours. Interacting with reporters on the sidelines of the forum, Malik, when asked about the role of culture in fostering better ties between India and Pakistan, said, "Culture has a very key role to play". Hours before the inauguration, the MEA on Friday said the forum was a "multilateral event within the SCO framework", for which invitations had been extended to all members of the grouping, including Pakistan. "India is hosting the 1st SCO Civilisation Dialogue on 20-22 November 2026, in New Delhi. This is a multilateral event within the SCO framework, for which invitations have been extended to all members of the SCO, including Pakistan," the MEA said in a post on X. "Observers and Dialogue Partners of the SCO have also been invited to attend the Dialogue, which will be inaugurated this evening by the Hon’ble Prime Minister," it said. The event is being hosted by the Ministry of Culture and the MEA. The SCO was founded at a summit in Shanghai in 2001 by the presidents of Russia, China, the Kyrgyz Republic, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. India and Pakistan became its permanent members in 2017.

stories.headline: India GDP growth projected at 7% for FY27
stories.title: India GDP growth projected at 7% for FY27
stories.summary: India’s real GDP growth is projected at about 7 per cent in FY27, Brickwork Ratings said, citing public capital expenditure, domestic demand and services, while forecasting a December 2026 repo rate hike amid inflation pressures.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: India’s real GDP growth is projected at about 7 per cent in FY27, Brickwork Ratings said, citing public capital expenditure, domestic demand and services, while forecasting a December 2026 repo rate hike amid inflation pressures.

Mumbai: India’s real GDP growth is projected at approximately 7 per cent for FY27, supported by sustained public capital expenditure, resilient domestic demand and strong services activity, according to a new Brickwork Ratings (BWR) report released on Saturday.

However, persistent inflationary pressures are expected to keep monetary policy tight, with BWR anticipating a further 25-basis-point (bps) repo rate hike in December 2026, taking the policy rate to 5.75 per cent, followed by an extended pause.
“India’s growth momentum is increasingly being supported by the strength of its domestic economy and the resilience of its services exports.
However, the external environment remains an important variable, particularly given India’s dependence on energy and other key imports,” said Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research, Brickwork Ratings.

In the current environment, businesses with healthy balance sheets, adequate liquidity and the ability to manage input-cost volatility will be better positioned to navigate uncertainty, the report said.
For the broader economy, sustaining investment momentum while strengthening external resilience will remain important, Sharan said.
Government capital expenditure reached Rs 6.55 lakh crore in the first half of FY27, supporting infrastructure investment, the report said.
Services activity remained robust, with the Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rising to 55.8 in October and the Composite PMI reaching 56.2.
Industrial production grew 6.7 per cent in September, while manufacturing output expanded 7.6 per cent.
October Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections also rose 22.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.31 lakh crore, reflecting festive demand and higher import-related collections.
Capital goods and electrical equipment, automobiles, IT services and export-oriented sectors are relatively better positioned, the report said.

stories.headline: 'Shocking The Conscience' Not Enough To Modify Arbitral Award: Supreme Court Restores Contractor's Claim Against Kolkata Port Trust
stories.title: 'Shocking The Conscience' Not Enough To Modify Arbitral Award: Supreme Court Restores Contractor's Claim Against Kolkata Port Trust
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has set aside a Calcutta High Court judgment that reduced an arbitral award in favour of a dredging contractor by 50%, holding that a court exercising jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, cannot interfere with an award merely because the amount granted for additional work appears excessive.

The Court held that the High Court's conclusion that the claim for additional work, which exceeded 70% of the original contract value, shocked its conscience was not a legally sustainable ground for modifying the award.

A bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran set aside a Calcutta High Court Division Bench order that had reduced the arbitral award by 50% on the ground that the amount awarded for additional work exceeded the original contract value by over 70%.

The Court noted that since the additional amount arose from repeated dredging undertaken by the contractor to keep the channel and basin operational, thus, the High Court had mechanically exercised its jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, to set aside the award on the mere ground that it exceeded the contract work value merely noting that it shocked the court's conscience without providing a “substantive reason which blatantly and patently brings forth the conflict with the most basic notions of morality or justice, resulting in the conscience of the Court being shocked.”

“…the impugned order has merely used the words on the sole ground of the bills for the additional work having exceeded 70% of the original contract; without looking at the nature of the additional work involved… The Division Bench considering the application under Section 37 has not looked into the measurement or the invoices, which in any event, would be an exercise of adjudication on merits, clearly prohibited under the Act of 1996.
The measurements and invoices raised are of one character, based on the additional work of redredging which cannot be compartmentalised as 'valid' and 'invalid'.”, the Court said.

The dispute arose from a contract awarded by the Kolkata Port Trust to Marino Dredgeco for dredging the riverbed and shores at Sagar Island to create an approach channel and basin for a pilot station.
During execution, repeated dredging became necessary due to siltation, adverse weather conditions, and differences between the actual soil conditions and the data supplied by the Port Trust.
The Port Trust also entrusted additional work through a letter dated July 19, 2000.
After completing the work, the contractor raised additional bills, which led to arbitration.
The Arbitrator awarded the claimed amounts, and the Single Judge upheld the award under Section 34.

However, the High Court Division Bench, in an appeal under Section 37, reduced the amount by 50% and reduced interest, reasoning that the additional-work claims exceeded 70% of the original contract value and shocked the Court's conscience, following which an appeal was filed by the award holder, Marino Dredgeco, before the Supreme Court.

The Port Trust also entrusted additional work through a letter dated July 19, 2000.
After completing the work, the contractor raised additional bills, which led to arbitration.
The Arbitrator awarded the claimed amounts, and the Single Judge upheld the award under Section 34.

The Supreme Court has set aside a Calcutta High Court judgment that reduced an arbitral award in favour of a dredging contractor by 50%, holding that a court exercising jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, cannot interfere with an award merely because the amount granted for additional work appears excessive.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Refuses Plea To Refer Shenbagavalli Weir Dispute Between Keralam & TN To Inter-State River Disputes Tribunal
stories.title: Supreme Court Refuses Plea To Refer Shenbagavalli Weir Dispute Between Keralam & TN To Inter-State River Disputes Tribunal
stories.summary: We cannot pass a mandamus initiating a litigation, said Justice Joymalya Bagchi.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: We cannot pass a mandamus initiating a litigation, said Justice Joymalya Bagchi.

The Supreme Court on Friday refused to entertain a plea seeking a direction to the Tamil Nadu government to refer the dispute concerning the restoration of the Shenbagavalli Weir and Kanyamadugu Channel to an Inter-State River Water Disputes Tribunal under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana declined to entertain the plea, which also sought judicial intervention to facilitate coordination between the two States for undertaking the restoration work.
Senior Advocate Srinath Sridevan appeared for the petitioner.

He submitted that the petitioner was seeking a mandamus to the Tamil Nadu government to make a request under Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 for reference of the issue to a Tribunal.
He argued that the Periyar river has been held to be an 'inter-state river' by the Supreme Court.
"There's a small check dam in the mountains where tributaries join the Periyar river..." the senior counsel was submitting when the CJI noted, "It's an inter-state dispute".
"We cannot pass a mandamus initiating a litigation" said Justice Bagchi.
When the bench asked the petitioner to approach the Tamil Nadu government, Sridevan submitted that the petitioner had already approached the state authorities.
Eventually, the matter was dismissed.

Briefly put, the petitioner, Ananthan Ayyasamy, sought directions to the states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala to jointly deliberate and arrive at an appropriate mechanism for restoring the functioning of the Shenbagavalli weir and repairing of the Kanyamadugu channel upto the TN border.

Alternatively, in case the concerned authorities failed to reach an agreement within a period stipulated by the Court, the petitioner sought a direction requiring Tamil Nadu government to submit a request to the Central Government under Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Seeks Centre's Stand on Genetic Risks of Consanguineous Marriages
stories.title: Supreme Court Seeks Centre's Stand on Genetic Risks of Consanguineous Marriages
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday sought a response from the Centre on a PIL seeking measures to raise awareness about the potential genetic and medical risks associated with consanguineous marriages (marriages between close blood relatives).

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that while marriage is a matter of personal choice and most of the reliefs sought fall within the legislative domain, the issue warrants greater public awareness.

The apex court issued notice to the Centre on a limited issue, specifically to ask the government to consider whether suitable legislation or awareness measures, including incorporating the subject into school and college curricula, were necessary to promote scientific understanding of the possible adverse effects of such marriages.

Justice Bagchi observed that individuals should be equipped to make an "informed decision" about consanguineous marriages, while referring to earlier judicial recognition of the right to marry an HIV-positive person with full knowledge of the condition.
The PIL was filed by Charvi S, a 20-year-old law student at the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, who has 40 per cent visual impairment.
She is herself the child of a first-cousin marriage and was diagnosed with cone dystrophy, an inherited eye disorder.

The petitioner contended that customary exceptions under Sections 5(iv) and 5(v) of the Hindu Marriage Act and Section 4(d) of the Special Marriage Act permit close-relative marriages despite the associated genetic risks.
She argued that the State must take preventive measures to protect the health and rights of future generations.

stories.headline: Maharashtra sees worst drought since 1972, Rabi sowing falls
stories.title: Maharashtra sees worst drought since 1972, Rabi sowing falls
stories.summary: Mumbai, Nov 21 : Maharashtra is facing one of its worst droughts in recent history, with Rabi sowing falling well below levels recorded during the devastating 1972 drought. According to the state Agriculture Department, only 14.74 lakh hectares have been sown so far in the 2026-27 Rabi season, compared with 47.29 lakh hectares during the 1972-73 season, raising fears that this could become the lowest Rabi sowing season on record in the state. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) and global weather organisations have declared the active El Niño in the Pacific Ocean to be a powerful "Super El Niño." Its direct impact on the monsoon led to a 19 per cent rainfall deficit across Maharashtra compared to the average, with Solapur recording the sharpest drop at 59 per cent below normal. Almost every district received deficient rainfall, and whatever rain did fall occurred largely within a 15-day window in July. Consequently, the Kharif season failed, and acute drinking water shortages in rural areas have slowed Rabi sowing to a crawl. The state Agriculture Department holds Rabi sowing records dating back to 1960. While Maharashtra's average Rabi sowing area is 55 to 60 lakh hectares, the historical comparison underscores the severity of the current crisis. "During the 1972-73 Rabi season, sowing for food grains was done on 36,64,000 hectares against 7,79,812 hectares this year, pulses 4,31,000 hectares against 6,78,385 hectares and oil seeds 6,34,000 hectares against paltry 16,106 hectares. Against the total sowing area of 47,29,000 hectares in 1972-73, only 14,74,304 hectares are there across the state in 2026-27," added the agriculture department. Previously, the lowest Rabi sowing in the state's history was recorded in 1991–92 at 40 lakh hectares. Experts see virtually no possibility of this year's total crossing the 20 to 25 lakh hectare mark by the end of December. "Farmers in the state are genuinely facing a severe drought situation. The Agriculture Department has appealed to farmers to cultivate fodder crops using whatever water is available for irrigation. Providing food grains to people is manageable, but supplying fodder and water for livestock is a massive challenge. The government and the Agriculture Department are planning meticulously to tackle the impending crisis," said the state Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharane. The drought has visibly disrupted rural life and impacted the Kartiki Yatra, a major pilgrimage of the Warkari sect. Anticipating a turnout of 12 to 15 lakh devotees, the local administration had made extensive arrangements in Pandharpur. However, only a little over 3 lakh devotees arrived in the temple town by Friday. The official Mahapuja was performed on Saturday by Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. Earlier, the Maharashtra Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Makarand Jadhav-Patil on November 19 announced that the state government has included six additional talukas in its list of drought-affected regions, taking the total number of drought-hit talukas in the state for the Kharif 2026 season to 310. The newly added talukas are Dindori (Nashik district), Wada and Vikramgad (Palghar district), Chiplun (Ratnagiri district), and Hatkanangale and Gadhinglaj (Kolhapur district). A Government Resolution (GR) formalising the decision has been issued. The state had earlier declared 304 talukas drought-affected based on rainfall deficit and other parameters during the 2026 Kharif season. Following representations seeking the inclusion of remaining affected areas, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis directed the administration during a recent Cabinet meeting to conduct a 20 per cent sample survey of five major crops and carry out on-ground field verification in accordance with Central government norms. Based on subsequent reports submitted by the respective District Collectors, these six talukas were added to the list, Minister Jadhav-Patil said. With this notification, a comprehensive package of drought relief measures and concessions has come into effect across the newly included talukas. Minister Jadhav-Patil said the government has provided exemptions in land revenue, restructuring of crop loans, and a stay on the recovery of agriculture-related loans. While agricultural pumps up to 7.5 horsepower (HP) already enjoy a full power bill waiver, pumps exceeding 7.5 HP in these talukas will receive concessions on current electricity bills. Furthermore, power connections to agricultural pumps in scarcity-declared villages will not be disconnected. ( IANS)
